slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single serialized image at EEPROM blocks 0-52. Loaded by 0x0800a198 on every main-loop iteration: if sum8+7 checksum at logical 422 matches and caller arg is 0, unpack via 0x08009168; otherwise discard and copy ROM defaults into RAM. No backup copy, mirror, generation counter, or A/B selection exists in the corpus.

slots_and_copies.name: unused_eeprom_tail

checksums.name: serialized_image_sum8_plus7
checksums.formula_detail: Logical (RAM) image viewed as 212 u16_le words: sum low byte of u16[0..210] (logical even bytes 0,2,...,420) modulo 256, plus 7, truncated to u8. Stored as low byte of u16 at logical offset 422 (0x1A6); high byte at 423 is 0x00 and ignored via &0xff. On-disk encoding: each 8-byte EEPROM block is byte-reversed between raw .sav and logical image, so the stored byte sits at raw file offset 0x1A1 and covered raw bytes are the per-block reversal of the logical even bytes. Code proof: 0x0800a198 loop for i<0xd3 c += *(char*)(i*2+buf), compare (c+7) vs *(u16*)(buf+0x1a6)&0xff.

io_driver_functions.notes: Save reader + verifier + default-reset. Allocates 424B via 0x08022554, brackets with 0x08000a8c/0x08000ac0, reads 53 EEPROM blocks of 8B via 0x08042aac(block, buf+block*8), verifies sum8+7 checksum, on pass calls external unpacker 0x08009168, on fail copies ROM defaults into 4x0x60 RAM profiles plus 5x0xC second struct. Caller edge is textual in 0x0800681c (func_0x0800a198(0) at decompiled.c:1296); callgraph.json lists no callers.

Indirect-jump thunk (jumptable not recovered). Called 53 times as (block_index 0..52, buf+block_index*8): per-8-byte EEPROM block read. Body not in corpus. CONFIRMED_STATIC call pattern; EEPROM-read role inferred from block size, reader context, and per-8-byte disk reversal verified against the sample.
Indirect-jump thunk called once as func_0x08042a94(4) before the block-read loop; return only logged via stub 0x08001db4. EEPROM library probe/configure role is HYPOTHESIS.

Bracket-close after EEPROM reads, before checksum: same shape as 0x08000a8c but second global gets a different value. Callgraph-confirmed sole caller 0x0800a198.

External (no body in 160-function corpus). func_0x08009168(serialized_buf) on checksum pass: unpacks 424B logical image into RAM profile array (4x0x60) and second struct (5x0xC RAM stride). Field-level unpack mapping inferred, not read.

External (no body in corpus). func_0x08009944() called once, immediately after 0x0800f648 writes a new RAM profile. Serialize+checksum+EEPROM-write flush by symmetry with the reader; writer internals HYPOTHESIS. Only proven EEPROM write trigger in the corpus.

fields.name: profile0_serialized_head
fields.update_mechanism: Packed by external serializer 0x08009944 from RAM profile slot 0 (RAM +0x00 u16 and +0x04 12xu32 are the known head fields); exact pack order unproven. Offsets in this JSON are logical/RAM-image offsets; raw .sav offset = (x & ~7) | (7 - (x & 7)).
fields.evidence: Serialized record size 0x44 proven by 0x44 periodicity of nonzero tails and 4*0x44=0x110 section closure in the sample; RAM head layout read in 0x0800a198 default-copy and 0x0800f648. Packer/unpacker bodies absent, all bytes zero in only sample, so internal mapping cannot be verified.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one bit in logical byte 0 (even, checksum-covered), no checksum repair. Convert via per-8B reversal before writing .sav.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Save rejected on reload from sav-00-pre.ss: profiles reset to ROM defaults, unpacker 0x08009168 not taken. Falsifies checksum coverage if it loads.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Same flip as above, then repair: ram[422]=(sum(ram[i*2] for i in range(211))+7)&0xff, re-encode per-8B reversal.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Loads as control; any visible/RAM difference isolates the mutated head field (compare RAM slot0 +0x00/+0x04 array).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one bit in logical byte 1 (odd logical offset, not summed by the checksum).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Loads exactly as control with unchanged checksum (verify in Python first). Rejection would refute the low-byte-only stride-2 checksum reading.
Loads as control: reader masks stored u16 with &0xff, so the high byte is ignored.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero the three 01 00 pairs at logical 52/54/56 of profile record 0 one at a time (repeat at +68 per record).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If RAM profile +0x4C/+0x4E/+0x50 move 1:1 after reload, the hypothesized tail-to-RAM pack mapping is confirmed; no movement refutes it.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Clear the 0x80 byte at record-relative +0x3B (logical 59 for record 0); separately set it in record 1.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Odd logical offset so checksum is unchanged. A profile appearing/disappearing or unlocking identifies a flag field (candidate RAM +0x54); no effect means it is part of a larger packed field.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change record 0 byte at logical 61 (record-relative +0x3D) from 0x41 to 0x42, then to 0x00.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Odd offset, no repair needed. If the displayed profile glyph changes (0x42 = next glyph) or the slot reads empty at 0x00, this byte is glyph-coded name data (candidate RAM +0x56); no change refutes that mapping.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change first byte of exactly one of the 15 second-section records (logical 272 + k*10) from 0x20 to 0x21.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Exactly one menu/title/riddle entry changes if records are independent; no visible change (or non-checksum rejection) shows the section is inert default data.
Profiles still load if the section is non-essential; a specific screen emptying/breaking identifies its consumer, then bisect per 10-byte record.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Overwrite raw .sav bytes 424-511 (EEPROM blocks 53-63, currently 0xFF) with 0x00, without touching the logical image.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Loads identically to control, proving the tail is unused. Any difference refutes the 53-block read bound.

open_questions: Body of serializer/EEPROM writer 0x08009944 is outside the 160-function corpus: exact RAM-to-serialized pack mapping (96B RAM profile -> 44B serialized record; 5x0xC RAM second struct -> 150B section) and its EEPROM write thunk are inferred from the reader, not read. A game-generated save after in-game profile creation (report fuzzing test 14) would settle the layout.

Body of unpacker 0x08009168 is absent: field-level deserialize mapping is inferred from 0x0800a198's default-copy layout and the sample's byte patterns, hence HYPOTHESIS confidence on pack correspondences (three 01 00 tail pairs vs RAM +0x4C/+0x4E/+0x50; 0x41 tail byte vs RAM +0x56 name; 0x80 tail byte vs RAM +0x54).

Numeric EWRAM/IWRAM base addresses of the profile array and second struct are unrecoverable from this corpus: Ghidra literal-pool placeholders (iRam0800a54c etc.) were never resolved to values and no ROM binary is in the workspace.
Purpose of bracket functions 0x08000a8c/0x08000ac0 around the EEPROM block reads, and of the 0x08042a94(4) library call, is unknown (thunk/library bodies absent).

Whether gameplay progression written to RAM by 0x0800681c and the external session functions (0x0800ad40, 0x0802c4d8, 0x08026d9c, 0x0801528c, 0x08013770) is flushed to EEPROM by 0x08009944 calls inside those external bodies, or only on profile creation, cannot be determined: the only traced 0x08009944 call site is profile creation in 0x0800f648.

Semantics of the 15 identical second-section records (bytes 20 49 50 53 00 59 00 00 00 00) and of serialized profile tail byte +0x3B (0x80) are unknown; the single sample is a near-blank/new-profile image with all gameplay fields zero, so counters/scores that only move in gameplay are indistinguishable from padding without the fuzzing plan in the report.

Only one .sav sample exists (frame 990, sav-00-f990.sav) and the paired states are identity metadata only (no .ss binaries in workspace), so multi-sample diffing and in-emulator reload verification could not be performed in this session.
